uceed-2018-q14:
The most private room is the one that takes the **most doors** to reach from the street. First find every gap in the outer walls (the entrances). Then, for each room, count the fewest doors needed to reach it from outside by the shortest route.

- **House 1–7:** 1, 3 and 5 open to the street. 2, 4, 6 and 7 are one room further in. Deepest is 2.
- **House 8–13:** 8, 10, 12 and 13 open to the street. 9 is reached through 10, and 11 through 12. Deepest is 2.
- **House 14–21:** 14, 17, 19, 20 and 21 open to the street. 18 is reached through 14, 15 through 19 and 16 through 20. Deepest is 2.
- **House 22–28:** 22, 26, 27 and 28 have street doors. 23 has none and is reached only from 22. 24 is reached only from 23, and 25 only from 24. The walls of 25 facing 26 and 28 are solid.

Route to 25: street → 22 → 23 → 24 → 25, which is 4 doors. No other room needs more than 2, so the answer is **25**.
uceed-2018-q28:
A rotation keeps every radial **stack** (outer band → second band → third band) together, and keeps the stacks in the same **clockwise order**. A mirror image keeps the stacks but reverses their order. So pick one stack, find it in each option, then walk clockwise.

In the figure, going clockwise from the top side, the stacks are:
- purple / dark green / purple → light blue / maroon / yellow → green / pink / purple → purple / dark green / red → peach / maroon / purple → green / pink / blue
- The centre triangles alternate red and green. The purple / dark green / purple side has a red triangle.

**D** has the purple / dark green / purple stack on its left side, with a red centre triangle. Going clockwise from there, every stack matches in order. It is the figure turned 90° anticlockwise, so **D** is correct.
- **A**: its upper-left stack is purple / dark green / **blue**. The figure has no such stack, because its blue sits inside green and pink.
- **B**: all the stacks are right, but they run anticlockwise, so it is a mirror image.
- **C**: its third band has two blue pieces, but the figure has only one.
uceed-2018-q44:
To estimate a pie chart, compare each slice with a **quarter** (90°, 25%). A 120° slice is **one-third**. Then add slices together and check them against **half** (180°).

- **Doctors** (blue) starts at 12 o'clock and ends before 3 o'clock, at about 72°: **≈20%**
- **Engineers** (red) runs from there to just past 6 o'clock, about 118°: **≈33%**
- **Businessmen** (green) is about the same size as blue, about 72°: **≈20%**
- **Designers** (purple) is slightly more than a quarter: **≈27%**

Checking the options:
- **A** is correct. Doctors and businessmen together are ≈40%, so blue and green fill clearly less than half the circle.
- **B** is correct. The red slice is about 120°, so it is roughly one-third.
- **C** is correct. Engineers and designers together are 33% + 27% ≈ 60%.
- **D** is wrong. It is the opposite of A.

**Answer: A, B, C**
uceed-2018-q48:
Update your heading after every turn: walking west, right is north; walking south, right is west. Count roads branching on the side you need; a sharp corner counts as a turn.
- West from Hampalkatte, the 1st right is the big curved road. The **2nd right** is the next road north, rising past the Dum Dum bend.
- Heading north, the 1st left is Sadashiv road. The **2nd left** is at the top, a short stretch west along the Hoskote road.
- That stretch bends sharply south: the **first left**.
- Heading south, you pass rights at Sadashiv and Hampalkatte roads; the bottom road is the **third right**.
- Heading west, the 1st left is the short diagonal. The **2nd left** is the curving road south. Follow it through Badi Chaudi to its end: **A. Kandivali**.

A right at the top junction leads to D (Hoskote). Skipping the last left, the bottom road ends at C (Navrangpura). B (Gurugram) is dead-end streets this route never enters.
uceed-2018-q62:
Mirroring across a shared edge sends each corner to the corner directly opposite it across that edge. So follow **one corner, the one holding the triangle**, from heptagon to heptagon. Don't jump ahead: each flip moves it somewhere different.

- Start: triangle sits in the **top-left corner** of the solid heptagon.
- Heptagon 2 (upper): it lands in the top-left corner.
- Heptagon 3 (lower): bottom-right corner.
- Heptagon 4 (upper): right end of the flat bottom edge.
- Heptagon 5: that corner is an end of the mirror edge, so the triangle stays put and becomes heptagon 5's left corner.
- Heptagon 6 (bottom): bottom-left corner.
- Heptagon 7 ("?"): **lower-right corner**, pointing inward.

**Answer: A**, which has the triangle in the lower-right corner.

- **B** puts it back in the starting corner. Six flips cancel the mirror-image effect, but they don't bring the triangle back to where it began.
- **C** (bottom-left) and **D** (upper-right) are corners the trace never reaches.
uceed-2018-q68:
Convert each hand to degrees per real time. The hour hand runs at half speed: **15° per hour**. The minute hand runs at 6× speed: 2160° per hour, or **36° per minute**.

- The hour hand points at **4** (120°): 120 ÷ 15 = **8 hours** after noon.
- The minute hand points at **6** (180°). 36 × 5 = 180°, and every 10 more minutes adds a full turn, so it is at 6 at 5, 15, 25 … minutes past each hour.
- At 8.00 the minute hand is at 12 (480 × 36° = 48 full turns). The next time it reaches 6 is **8.05**, when the hour hand is at 121°, just past 4. Answer: **C**.

All four options put the minute hand at 6, so the hour hand decides:
- **A** (8.45): 131°, a third of the way to 5.
- **B** (9.05): 136°, past halfway to 5.
- **D** (10.15): 154°, past 5.
